diagnosis_explanation: Your pancreas has a growth. This growth has spread to your liver. This is called liver metastases. It also caused diabetes. Diabetes means your blood sugar is too high. High blood pressure is also a problem.
medication_rationale:
Phenergan 25 mg q.6. as needed:
This medicine helps with nausea and vomiting. It can also make you feel sleepy. You may feel drowsy. This is a common effect. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you get a rash.

Duragesic patch 100 mcg q.3.d.:
This medicine is a strong pain reliever. It is a patch you wear on your skin. It helps control your pain. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is normal. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you feel very confused.

Benadryl 25-50 mg by mouth four times daily:
This medicine is for itching. It helps stop your skin from feeling itchy. You may feel drowsy from this medicine. Taking it may make your mouth dry. Call your doctor if your itching gets worse. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Enalapril - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine. It was helping your high blood pressure. Do not take it until your doctor tells you it is safe to start again.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and sore after your procedure.
- Rest is important for healing.
- Do not do strenuous activity.
- Eat your regular diet as advised by Dr. X.
- Your goal is to rest and move around your home slowly.
- Call your doctor if you have fever or worsening pain.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a bit more energy this week.
- You can do light activities around the house.
- Avoid any heavy lifting or hard exercise.
- Continue to eat your regular diet.
- Your goal is to walk a little more each day.
- Call your doctor if your pain gets worse.

**Week 3:**
- You might feel stronger and have more energy now.
- You can try doing more of your regular activities.
- Make sure to avoid any strenuous activity.
- Eat your regular diet as usual.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes without stopping.
- Call your doctor if you develop a fever.

**Week 4:**
- Many people feel much better by this week.
- You can slowly return to most of your normal activities.
- Do not do any heavy lifting or very hard exercise.
- Continue to eat your regular diet.
- Your goal is to walk outside for short periods.
- Call your doctor if your pain returns or gets worse.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel a steady improvement each week.
- Keep following Dr. X's advice on diet and activity.
- Watch for signs of stent problems like fever or pain.
- Healing is a process that takes time.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Stent occlusion: Blood flow is blocked. This is an emergency.
- Fever: Your body may have a bad infection.
- Increased bilirubin: Your liver or bile duct is blocked.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Worsening pain: Your pain is not controlled.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.
